question: A circuit consisting of an NTC-type thermistor and a fixed resistor is connected in series with a DC power supply. What change will occur in the output voltage as the temperature increases?

options.text: The output voltage will remain constant.
The value of the output voltage will fluctuate depending on the resistor value.

solution:
The correct answer is __The output voltage will increase****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NTC-type thermistor__ refers to a thermistor with a Negative Temperature Coefficient.
 
• As the temperature increases, the resistance of the NTC thermistor decreases.
 
• In a series circuit with a fixed resistor, the voltage across the fixed resistor will increase as the thermistor's resistance decreases.
 
• This leads to an increase in the output voltage of the circuit.
 
• The relationship between temperature and resistance in an NTC thermistor is inversely proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermistors:**
 
 
• Thermistors are temperature-sensitive resistors.
 
• They are classified into two types: NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) and PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient).
 
 
 
• **Fixed Resistors:**
 
 
• Fixed resistors have a constant resistance value that does not change with temperature or voltage.
 
• They are used to control the voltage and current in a circuit.
 
 
 
• **DC Power Supply:**
 
 
• Provides a steady direct current (DC) voltage to electrical circuits.
 
• Used in various applications, including powering resistive and thermistor-based circuits.
